Students learn the basics of three-dimensional and computer-aided rendering, rapid idea generation, and object design principles through the lens of contemporary examples during the first segment of the course. During the second part of the curriculum, these new skills are applied to design and build a programmable LED Glowing Object. The design process builds upon knowledge from the first part of the semester, utilizing hand drawing and rapid design visualization before moving into detailed digital modeling. Students must use the materials, tools, and techniques of multiple shop disciplines during the class's fabrication portion: metal, wood, plastics, fabrics, electronics, programming, and digital fabrication.  This course, taken concurrently with Contemporary Media & Art (Visual Arts Department), is required of all 9th graders and is a prerequisite for further work in the Technical Arts Department. Prerequisite: None This is a yearlong course and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: for further work in the Technical Arts Department.

courses.title: Graphics and Game Design
courses.brief_description: Creative, innovative, and practical applications of computer programming
courses.description: This course introduces students to creative, innovative, and practical applications of computer programming. In the first of two projects, students use generative drawing techniques to design graphic patterns for a textile, which then becomes physical as we digitally print and sew an object from the code-created fabric. The project explores visual principles like color theory alongside programming fundamentals, including control flow, data types, variables, functions, arrays, and randomization. In the second project, students use object-oriented programming to design and build a unique browser-based game. Throughout the course, we use pair programming as well as formal and informal feedback sessions to create a social, collaborative, and inclusive classroom community.     The syllabus is project-based and requires no previous background—we begin with the basics. Students with prior experience are equally welcome and will have the opportunity to stretch their knowledge through interest-driven projects and through connections to other disciplines.  This class meets the Tech Arts “Design & Engineering” category requirement. Prerequisite: Design & Technology This semester long course is offered in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 and is UC approved.

courses.title: Jewelry 1
courses.brief_description: Metalsmithing, jewelry, and creative craftsmanship
courses.description: In this course, students learn traditional techniques of metalsmithing and jewelry using copper, brass, and sterling silver. Students are introduced to a number of techniques for cutting metal, cold methods of joinery, soldering, forming, as well as various means of surface textures and treatments. The design process will be emphasized through research, drawing and working closely with the teacher to develop and expand ideas. Creativity and innovation are fostered and encouraged. As the class progresses, students will better recognize the value of craftsmanship as they create their own skillfully crafted, one of a kind, wearable art. This class meets the “Design & Craft” category requirement. Prerequisite: Design and Technology This course is offered in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 and is UC approved.

courses.title: Jewelry 2
courses.brief_description: Metalwork, soldering, and stone setting
courses.description: In addition to refining the techniques learned in Jewelry 1, this course will expose students to more complex technical processes, such as chain making, stone setting, and enameling. As students become more confident with soldering and other smithing techniques, they will begin to gain the confidence to create a wide range of objects and realize more complex designs. Craftsmanship and design will be emphasized through a series of projects aimed to challenge students while they create one of a kind wearable art. This semester-long course can be repeated and offers a modified curriculum to challenge more advanced students. This class meets the “Design & Craft” category requirement. Prerequisites: Design & Technology and Jewelry 1 This course is offered in Fall 2026 and is UC approved.

courses.title: Private Skills for a Public Purpose PPP
courses.brief_description: Build skills while fulfilling local partner organizations' needs
courses.description: Private Skills for a Public Purpose (PSPP) aims, through design and research, to allow our students to examine their privileges and biases and, more importantly, the role we all play in the larger education system. Students mix reading and research with tangible, hands-on shop skills to build relationships and foster empathy for people beyond the school walls. Shop skills are primarily in wood and metal fabrication; however, specific tools or mediums do not constrain the course. Students have the opportunity to work closely with a public school or nonprofit organization to provide design and build skills while filling needs within the local organizations. The course begins with an in-depth inquiry into systematic social inequities and challenges students to think about their privileged position. The rest of the course focuses on designing and building projects to meet the organization's and stakeholders' needs. This course is an ideal opportunity for students to learn about the client/builder relationship through site visits, interviews, and observations about the organization's needs. The experience culminates in the delivery of the finished projects. This class meets the Tech Arts "Design & Engineering" category requirement. Prerequisite: Design & Technology This UC approved semester long course is offered in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 and fulfills the Public Purpose Program requirement for juniors and seniors.

courses.title: Advanced Architectural Design
courses.brief_description: Socially responsible and sustainable architecture
courses.description: A continuation and extension of the introductory Architectural Design class, the Advanced Architectural Design course is designed to make connections with the real world. While students still explore the value of creativity and originality of their designs, a great emphasis is placed on learning about socially responsible and sustainable architecture. Additionally, students study the technological, ecological, and urban aspects of skyscrapers because they have fundamentally transformed cities. No other form of construction can replace them as a response to the exponentially increasing need for space. In order to deepen their sense of architectural composition while developing a personal style, students work on individual and group projects. Their studio work is supplemented with slides and film presentations that address issues in contemporary architecture. Class activities include oral and written critiques in response to student and professional work, visits to exhibits and design studios, and presentations by local professionals. Prerequisite: Architectural Design or permission from the instructor. This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: Architectural Design or permission from the instructor.

courses.title: Architectural Design
courses.brief_description: The principles of architectural composition
courses.description: Students will explore the world of their imagination as they learn the principles of architectural composition. The course will address foundations of the design process such as form, function, proportion, scale, and space. Through a number of individual projects, students learn about specific requirements for the design of private and public spaces. Great emphasis is placed on creativity, graphic presentation, and computer skills. In addition, students practice hand sketching and coloring, as well as model making. Studio work is supplemented by a survey of important monuments in the history of architecture, guest appearances by local architects, and field trips to design studios. Prerequisite: Contemporary Media and Art This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.

courses.title: Architectural Design 3
courses.brief_description: A deeper analysis of the architectural world
courses.description: A continuation and extension of the Advanced Architectural Design, this course is designed to make deeper connections with the world of architecture. Students are given an opportunity to explore topics in the field of their interest. They continue to examine the rich and imaginative accomplishments in contemporary architecture. They develop creative ways to solve the problems of defining and organizing space while satisfying the functional and technical requirements. The work can be design or research based. The final product can vary from models and drawings to articles and journals. Their studio work is supplemented with slides and film presentations. Class activities include oral and written critiques in response to student and professional work, visits to exhibits and design studios, and presentations by local professionals. Prerequisite: Advanced Architectural Design This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.

courses.title: Art in Action PPP
courses.brief_description: Changemaking through the language of art
courses.description: Changemaking through the language of art This class explores and examines how to use the language of art, via multimedia, to create change in the world. Topics covered include how the language of art influences social interactions through films, podcasting, and graphic design. Students will learn to create a socially engaged art practice, how to construct influence in the digital world, skills for effective visual communication, and media production to disseminate ideas. An examination of artworks that spurred cultural change, along with class field trips and guest visits with contemporary artists, will guide us in the making of our own original artwork.   Prerequisite: Contemporary Media and Art This semester long course is offered in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 and fulfills the Public Purpose Program requirement for juniors and seniors. It is a UC approved course.

courses.title: Contemporary Media and Art
courses.brief_description: Architecture, Collage, Digital Photography, Drawing, Film, and Painting
courses.description: All LWHS students take this energetic, multidisciplinary arts class. Contemporary Media and Art is a course in Architecture, Collage, Digital Photography, Drawing, Film, and Painting where students get experience in a wide variety of visual languages and exposure to the practice and history of each medium. Students work in traditional and digital media, learning how it can be used to create compelling and meaningful artwork. Class projects are thematically based. Students develop creative and personal expressions in response to relevant social matters, individual interests and experience, as well as explorations of design, composition and form. We strive to embolden all 9th graders in their abilities in the visual arts. To that aim, students actively keep a visual journal for projects and experimentation. Through their work, 9th graders expand their knowledge about art and enhance their appreciation of its role in society. During the year, students use the habits of mind through imagination, expression, and reflection. With inquiry, effort, and perseverance students grow as artists, thinkers, and people. Prerequisite: None  This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.

courses.title: Drawing & Painting
courses.brief_description: Drawing & painting through observation and analysis of the physical world
courses.description: The premise of this class is that drawing and painting are learnable skills through which one is able to connect with and express the creativity that lies within. This class teaches students to draw and paint through exercises that train them in observation and analysis of the physical world. Students study the foundations of realist art and begin to explore connections with abstract art, and art inspired by the imagination. Students forge competency in art skills through assignments that cover various techniques and materials that are designed to promote and encourage growth in creative interpretation and nurture individual style. They are expected to explore ideas and methods that may be new and challenging, that may lead to personal discoveries. The successful student strives for both technical proficiency and creative expression. Pedagogy will include demonstrations, critiques and discussions, field trips, as well as video and slide presentations. Prerequisites: Contemporary Media and Art This semester long course is offered in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 and is UC approved.

courses.title: Film 1: Cinematic Storytelling PPP
courses.brief_description: The art of filmmaking with a focus on storytelling
courses.description: In this class, students will have the opportunity to delve into the art of filmmaking while shining a focused spotlight on storytelling. Students will have the opportunity to develop their own original short films and learn specific techniques, including the visual language of film, character development, and dramatic motivation. Students will hone their shooting skills and cinematography with in-class exercises, create original screenplays and storyboards, and learn techniques to improve workflow during digital video editing. The art of sound design and lighting will also be introduced. The point of view of both the filmmaker and the audience will be examined. Students will watch and analyze a diverse array of exemplary films. Prerequisite: Contemporary Media and Art This semester long course is offered in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 and fulfills the Public Purpose Program requirement for juniors and seniors. It is a UC approved course.

courses.title: Film 2: Advanced Film Studio
courses.brief_description: A continuation and extension of the Film 1: Cinematic Storytelling PPP class
courses.description: The Advanced Film Studio course is designed to make deeper connections with the art of filmmaking. Students will have the opportunity to explore topics in their field of interest, growing their personal style and artistic vision. Motion effects and graphics, keyframing, mattes, multiple camera editing, advanced audio production, LUTs color grading, dynamic image movement, and animation will also be introduced. Emphasizing individual creativity and collaborative work, students will hone their camera skills, create screenplays and storyboards, develop and manage their principal photography projects, and learn techniques to improve workflow during editing. Manipulation of the visual language of film, intention, impact, and meaning will be explored. Prerequisite: Film 1: Cinematic Storytelling PPP This course is offered in Spring 2027 and is UC approved.

courses.title: Photography 1
courses.brief_description: Foundational skills in digital single-lens reflex camera, Photoshop & digital printing
courses.description: This class is an introduction to photography, emphasizing both art and technique. It covers basic skills in the use of a manual 35mm film camera and beginning darkroom processes. It will also cover digital techniques, including basic Photoshop adjustments, and digital printing. Assignments will focus on building technical skill and exploring your personal voice through the medium of photography. Some topics include portraiture, landscape, and pinhole photography. The course will expose students to contemporary and historic photographic work and invite reflection and growth through critique and revision. Coursework considers the qualities of photography as a visual art and as a means of creative communication. Prerequisite: Contemporary Media and Art This semester long course is offered in both Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 and is UC approved.

courses.title: Accelerated Spanish 2
courses.brief_description: Enhance communicative skills with a focus on vocabulary expansion
courses.description: Accelerated Spanish 2 is designed for students who have demonstrated a mastery of the grammar and vocabulary of Spanish 1 in both their written and oral communications. In this course, students enhance their communicative skills with a focus on vocabulary expansion, hone their skills in applying the grammar they learned in Spanish 1, and gain an understanding of the uses of the indicative past tenses and approach to other advanced conjugations. The textbook Enfoques and teacher-generated materials are the primary resources. Students read several readers in Spanish, create their own stories, listen to and discuss music, view and analyze short films, and work collaboratively on many different group projects to enhance their oral, listening, and writing skills. The class is primarily conducted in Spanish. Prerequisites: Spanish 1 students who have met the grade requirements for entrance into this class. Incoming students must take a written and oral placement examination. This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: Spanish 1 students who have met the grade requirements for entrance into this class. Incoming students must take a written and oral placement examination.

courses.title: Chinese 1
courses.brief_description: Develop foundational Chinese skills
courses.description: Chinese 1 is the foundation course for the study of Mandarin Chinese. It is designed for students who have had little or no previous study of the language. Through various classroom activities and projects, students develop all four language skills including listening, speaking, reading and writing(simplified characters) in basic Mandarin Chinese on daily life topics such as family, time and school life. The textbook Integrated Chinese volume 1 is the primary resource, along with other supplementary listening and reading materials. This course prepares the students to achieve a proficiency level of Novice-mid to Novice-High across interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational communications (based on the ACTFL standards) at the end of the school year. Mandarin Chinese is the primary language of instruction. Prerequisite: None  This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.

courses.title: Chinese 2
courses.brief_description: Build upon the foundations developed in Chinese 1
courses.description: Chinese 2 builds upon and extends the foundations developed in Chinese 1. Language skills and cultural knowledge are broadened and deepened with more topics introduced. Topics include but are not limited to shopping, transportation, weather, seeing a doctor etc. Students will also be introduced to the culture via supplemental readings and listening materials, while the textbook Integrated Chinese volume 1 & 2 serves as the primary resource. This course prepares the students to achieve a proficiency level of Novice-high to Intermediate-low across interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational communications (based on the ACTFL standards) at the end of the school year. Mandarin Chinese is the sole language of instruction. Prerequisites: Chinese 1. Incoming students must take a placement examination and be interviewed. This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: Chinese 1. Incoming students must take a placement examination and be interviewed.

courses.title: Chinese 3
courses.brief_description: Expressions, styles, and language structures of higher complexity in both oral and written communication forms
courses.description: Chinese 3 builds upon and extends the foundations developed in Chinese 2. Its primary focus is to equip the students with expressions, styles, and language structures of higher complexity in both oral and written communication forms. Students continue to refine reading and writing using all modes. This course prepares the students to achieve a proficiency level of Intermediate-low to Intermediate-mid across interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational communications (based on the ACTFL standards) at the end of the school year. Topics include but are not limited to living space, sports, travel, academic planning, and education systems. The course will follow Integrated Chinese Volume 2 &3  and other supplementary materials. Correlated cultural topics are introduced with each unit for further exploration and comparisons. Mandarin Chinese is the sole language of instruction. Prerequisites: Chinese 2. Incoming students must take a placement examination. This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: Chinese 2. Incoming students must take a placement examination.

courses.title: French 1
courses.brief_description: Develop foundational French skills
courses.description: French I is the foundation course for the study of French, designed for students who have had no previous study of the language, or not quite enough to have placed into French 2.  Students acquire essential vocabulary through stories and through verbal, audio, visual, and tactile modes, movement, music and rhythm, and interactive games. These multi-sensory strategies increase retention.  We build intercultural competency through the exploration of many francophone cultures and learn to communicate in a variety of contexts, including but not limited to, sharing personal information, school, leisure-time activities, family, fashion and clothing, and technology.  The primary focus is on comprehensible communication, and grammar is scaffolded to support that goal. Students are able to write basic sentences, personal paragraphs, story summaries, and original stories. .   Prerequisites: None This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.

courses.title: French 2
courses.brief_description: Speak more creatively and spontaneously in French
courses.description: In French 2, we continue our language proficiency journey.  Students begin to transition from speaking with memorized structures toward speaking more creatively and spontaneously in French, expanding themes to move beyond their immediate world.  We review French 1 thoroughly before developing communication and intercultural skills around the themes of travel and language, family and relationships,  personal style, and other topics.  We continue to explore deeper the many Francophone cultures of Europe, Africa, the Americas, and the South Pacific. We communicate in the present, past, and future, as well as begin to use more advanced structures. Prerequisites: French 1. Incoming students must take a written and oral placement examination. This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: French 1. Incoming students must take a written and oral placement examination.

courses.title: French 3
courses.brief_description: Explore francophone cultures through thematic stories and other media
courses.description: In French 3, students continue to develop language proficiency as they explore francophone cultures through thematic stories and other media.  We examine art in our daily lives and as a reflection of culture, borders and migration, climate and environment, and other topics.  Students create more with the language as they expand their ability to communicate in personal, social, and other contexts.  Basic grammar is reviewed and refined in the context of these themes, and more advanced structures, such as the conditional and subjunctive verb tenses, are used.  Students expand and refine their writing through the use of transitional devices and the practice of both formal and informal correspondence.   Prerequisites: French 2. Incoming students must take a written and oral placement examination. This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: French 2. Incoming students must take a written and oral placement examination.

courses.title: Honors Chinese 4
courses.brief_description: Communicate in great depth about everyday activities, current events, and culture
courses.description: Honors Chinese 4 extends the foundation developed in previous levels and improves students' ability to communicate in the context of contemporary Chinese culture. Students analyze readings in the textbook, as well as historical idiom stories and classic novels. Students communicate in great depth about everyday activities, current events, and culture. Students further expand on their abilities to read and write in all modes. Topics include but are not limited to the course selection, computer and Internet usages, working part-time, education, geography of China, various idiom stories, etc.  The course will follow Integrated Chinese Volume 3  and other supplementary materials. Correlated cultural topics are introduced with each unit for further exploration and comparisons. This course prepares the students to achieve a proficiency level of Intermediate-mid to Intermediate-high across interpretive, interpersonal, and presentational communications (based on the ACTFL standards) at the end of the school year. Mandarin Chinese is the sole language of instruction. Prerequisites: Chinese 3 students who have met the requirements for entrance into Chinese Honors 4. Any new student to the Chinese program must take a placement examination. This course is offered yearlong and is UC approved.
courses.prerequisites: Chinese 3 students who have met the requirements for entrance into Chinese Honors 4. Any new student to the Chinese program must take a placement examination.

courses.title: Honors Chinese 5/6 PPP
courses.brief_description: Explore China's past and present, through reading, research, writing essays, and more
courses.description: This advanced course is designed for students who have reached an intermediate-high to advanced-low level of proficiency in listening, reading, writing, and speaking Chinese. With emphasis on thematic units, students will explore China’s past and present,  through reading, research, writing essays, giving presentations and engaging in daily discussions using critical thinking, comparing, and contrasting.  Authentic materials will be used as the primary resource. Mandarin Chinese is the sole language of instruction.  This combo course is on a two-year cycle. Each year, we will work with different curriculums and projects, therefore CHI 6H is not a repeat of CHI 5H.    The public purpose program (PPP) component will align with the curriculum to guide students to apply their knowledge to the actions,  then ultimately bring positive change to the community around them. Prerequisite: Honors Chinese 4 or Honors Chinese 5 students who have met the requirements for entrance into Honors Chinese 5/Honors Chinese 6. Any new student to the Chinese program must take a placement examination. This UC approved course is offered yearlong and fulfills the Public Purpose Program requirement for juniors and seniors.
courses.prerequisites: Honors Chinese 4 or Honors Chinese 5 students who have met the requirements for entrance into Honors Chinese 5/Honors Chinese 6. Any new student to the Chinese program must take a placement examination.
